title: Erdős #124: Sharpness of the Completeness Condition at a Single Base
description: At the single-base boundary k = 1, the Erdős #124 sufficient condition ∑ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 — proved sufficient in the parent — is shown to be necessary and sufficient: every natural number is 0/1-representable in base d iff d = 2 iff 1/(d−1) ≥ 1, with the number 2 an explicit obstruction in every base d ≥ 3.

meta.author: Burr–Erdős–Graham–Li (1996); formalization: Lean Genius Researcher
meta.assumptions: Fully machine-checked, 0 sorries, 0 axiom declarations; all theorems depend only on the foundational axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool — kernel-verified, no native_decide). Honest scope: this proves the CONVERSE (necessity) of the Erdős #124 condition only at the single-base boundary k = 1, where it becomes an exact characterisation. It does NOT prove general (k ≥ 2) necessity, which is the delicate asymptotic density statement of Burr–Erdős–Graham–Li and is not attempted here.
originalContributions: single_base_complete_iff_sum_cond: at k = 1 the Erdős sum condition 1 ≤ 1/(d−1), proved SUFFICIENT in the parent, is necessary AND sufficient for completeness
zeroOne_all_iff_two: for a single base d ≥ 2, every n is 0/1-representable in base d ⇔ d = 2
not_zeroOne_two_of_three_le: the explicit obstruction — for every base d ≥ 3 the number 2 fails (its only base-d digit is 2 ∉ {0,1})
zeroOne_base_two: base-2 completeness (every n has 0/1 binary digits), the d = 2 instance
sum_cond_iff_two: the threshold algebra 1 ≤ 1/(d−1) ⇔ d = 2 for d ≥ 2

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #124 (Burr, Erdős, Graham, Li, 1996; solved and formally verified by Harmonic's Aristotle in November 2025) asks when a family of bases yields a complete digit system. The parent gallery entry (Erdos124CompleteSequences.lean) formalizes the sufficient direction: if every dᵢ ≥ 2 and ∑ᵢ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1, then every natural number n is a sum ∑ᵢ aᵢ where each aᵢ has only the digits 0 and 1 in base dᵢ. Whether the hypothesis ∑ᵢ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 is necessary is a natural follow-up; in general it is a subtle density question, but at the single-base boundary k = 1 it admits a clean, fully verified resolution.
overview.problemStatement: Is the Erdős #124 sum condition ∑ᵢ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 necessary for completeness? Restricting to a single base (k = 1), the representation n = ∑ᵢ aᵢ forces a = n, so completeness in base d means precisely that every natural number already has only 0/1 digits in base d. For which bases d does this hold, and how does that relate to the threshold 1/(d−1) ≥ 1?
overview.proofStrategy: Work with the parent's per-base predicate ZeroOne d a := (Nat.digits d a).toFinset ⊆ {0,1}. Base 2 is complete because every binary digit is < 2 (zeroOne_base_two via Nat.digits_lt_base). For d ≥ 3 the digits of 2 are exactly [2] (digits_two_of_three_le, via Nat.digits_def'), so 2 is not 0/1-representable (not_zeroOne_two_of_three_le) — a single explicit counterexample. These combine into zeroOne_all_iff_two: completeness ⇔ d = 2. Independently, the Erdős sum at k = 1 is 1/(d−1), and elementary algebra gives sum_cond_iff_two: 1 ≤ 1/(d−1) ⇔ d = 2 for d ≥ 2. Chaining the two equivalences yields single_base_complete_iff_sum_cond: at the boundary the Erdős condition is necessary and sufficient.
keyInsights: At a single base the abstract completeness condition collapses to a concrete digit condition: n is representable iff n itself has 0/1 digits, so completeness means every n does — which is exactly the defining property of base 2.

The failure for d ≥ 3 is witnessed by the single smallest non-trivial number, 2: in any base d ≥ 3 it is one digit long and that digit is 2, outside {0,1}. No asymptotics are needed to see the threshold is sharp.
The arithmetic threshold matches the digit threshold exactly: 1/(d−1) ≥ 1 ⇔ d ≤ 2 ⇔ d = 2 (for d ≥ 2), so the parent's sufficient inequality is, at k = 1, the precise dividing line.
This is the converse half the parent leaves open; the general k ≥ 2 necessity is a genuine density argument and is deliberately not claimed here.

conclusion.summary: At the single-base boundary k = 1, the Erdős #124 sum condition ∑ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 — proved sufficient in the parent — is shown to be necessary and sufficient for completeness: every natural number is 0/1-representable in base d iff d = 2 iff 1/(d−1) ≥ 1. The obstruction for d ≥ 3 is the single explicit number 2. The proof is fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms beyond Mathlib's foundational three.
conclusion.implications: This pins the Erdős #124 threshold exactly at the only base where it can be tested in isolation, confirming the parent's inequality is the precise dividing line and not merely sufficient. It isolates which part of the general necessity question is elementary (the boundary) from which is genuinely hard (the k ≥ 2 density statement).
openQuestions: Is the condition ∑ᵢ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 necessary for completeness when k ≥ 2 (the general Burr–Erdős–Graham–Li density question), and can the standard counting/density argument be formalized?
For two bases, what is the exact set of pairs (d₁, d₂) that are complete, and does it coincide with 1/(d₁−1) + 1/(d₂−1) ≥ 1 with no exceptional small cases?
Can the single-base obstruction (the number 2) be sharpened to an explicit smallest non-representable value as a function of the base family in the incomplete regime?

crossReferences.description: The parent formalizes the SUFFICIENT direction of Erdős #124 (∑ 1/(dᵢ−1) ≥ 1 ⟹ completeness). This child proves the CONVERSE at the single-base boundary k = 1, where the condition becomes necessary and sufficient, with the number 2 as the explicit obstruction for d ≥ 3.

A complementary necessity result: erdos-124-complete-sequences-oq-02 establishes the general counting/density obstruction (N ≤ ∏ 2^{Lᵢ(N)}) across many bases. This entry instead pins the exact threshold at the single-base boundary k = 1 with an explicit finite obstruction (the number 2), giving a sharp iff rather than an asymptotic bound.
